findings.claim: The packet omits the native definition syntax and supporting contract receipts needed to independently review its five-harness installation claim.
findings.evidence: The intent requires native definitions for Codex, Claude, Kimi, OpenCode and MiniMax. The packet contains the canonical manifest and ten documentation/launcher artifacts, but no .codex/agents, .claude/agents, .kimi-code/agents, .opencode/agents or .minimax/agents file contents. verification.nativeSyntaxSummary asserts count=50 and allSyntaxAndPromptsPassed=true while referring to an external verification.json; research.harness similarly refers to research/uar-harness-research.md without supplying its contents. Factoring repeated prompts preserves prompt text but does not expose native headers, permission fields, serialization or the contract evidence used to validate them. Consequently this packet-only review cannot independently assess those installation details.
findings.suggested_fix: Include each distinct native definition envelope with its canonical prompt reference and role-specific fields, together with the native contract excerpts and per-harness validation receipts, or explicitly restrict this review's certification to the included manifest, documentation and launcher. Keep native activation and inference marked unverified where they were not run.

checked_classes: Requirement coverage: explicit product and UX roles, graph-based routing, planned UAR contracts, peer handoffs and five named harness targets are present; native serialization evidence is limited by the reported warning.

Ownership and dependencies: default write paths are disjoint in the supplied manifest; shared composition roots, contracts, tests and uncovered services require exact lead assignment; product and UX handoffs precede applicable implementation.

Source-evidence overclaim: repository-map separates planned UAR integration from observed DSH integration, identifies partial graph coverage and declines unsupported cross-package and cross-repository call claims. Source receipts themselves are not in the packet and were not independently verified.

Authority and trust boundaries: peer writes, external communications and publication require task authorization; model prompts and ownership are explicitly distinguished from native permission enforcement.

Usability and verification: actual Electron, keyboard, accessibility and platform evidence is required at completed boundaries; unavailable checks remain gaps; static installation does not claim application acceptance.
Review independence: review protocol permits an explicitly weaker fresh-context same-family fallback; the supplied gateway timeout does not claim a judge verdict or cross-model pass.

Launcher and portability: included launcher computes project-relative root and MiniMax data paths, forwards arguments and reports absent executables; native CLI execution and cross-platform activation were not performed in this artifact-only review.
limitations: Judged only the supplied final-packet.json and reviewer mandate; did not inspect implementation, external sources or omitted receipts.
REST MiniMax timed out and native Kimi failed account entitlement according to the task metadata. This GPT-6-family review is a weaker same-family fallback, not a cross-model pass.
PASS means no evidence-backed CRITICAL finding in the supplied artifacts; it does not certify omitted native definitions, runtime invocation, application behavior or customer acceptance.
